cards.explanation: The answer is to satisfy their hunger. The LORD asks if Job can hunt the prey for a lioness or "…satisfy the hunger of young lions" (Job 38:39). These cubs are crouched in their dens, just lying in wait. Feeding that crowd is a full-time job, friends, and I think I'd last about a day.
The answer is God. The text says the raven's young "…cry out to God as they wander about for lack of food?" (Job 38:41). The LORD asks who provides food for the raven. God is the One they cry out to.

The answer is False. The young goats and fawns thrive and grow up in the open field, and then "they leave and do not return." (Job 39:4). No coming back for Sunday dinner, friends. They're out there on their own.
The answer is True. The LORD tells Job, "I made the wilderness his home and the salt flats his dwelling." (Job 39:6). That's a pretty big backyard for one donkey.

The answer is False. The wild donkey "…scorns the tumult of the city and never hears the shouts of a driver." (Job 39:7). No traffic, no honking, no one yelling at him to hurry up. Honestly, friends, that sounds peaceful.

The answer is that Job can't make him do that. The LORD asks if the wild ox will consent to serve Job, stay by his manger at night, or plow the valleys behind him (Job 39:9-10). Each question points to the same answer: Job can't make him. I've had a hard enough time getting a cookie to stay in the shape I stamped it.
The answer is strength. The LORD asks, "Can you rely on his great strength?" (Job 39:11). That ox has plenty of strength, friends. The question is whether Job can leave his hard work to him.

The answer is False. The text says she "…forgets that a foot may crush them, or a wild animal may trample them." (Job 39:15). She leaves her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the sand (Job 39:14). Forgetting is exactly what the verse says she does.

The answer is wisdom. The LORD says, "…God has deprived her of wisdom; He has not endowed her with understanding." (Job 39:17). That's the word right there, friends. It sits right after the part about her treating her young harshly.

The answer is the horse and its rider. When she proudly spreads her wings, "…she laughs at the horse and its rider." (Job 39:18). That's a whole horse and a whole rider, friends, and she laughs at both. Quite the confidence.
The answer is laughs. The war horse "…laughs at fear, frightened of nothing…" (Job 39:22). He doesn't turn back from the sword either. That's one fearless horse, friends.

The answer is the ram's horn. The war horse "…cannot stand still when the ram’s horn sounds." (Job 39:24). Then at the blast of the horn, he snorts with fervor (Job 39:25). This horse hears that sound and he's gone.

The answer is True. The text says, "He catches the scent of battle from afar, the shouts of captains and the cry of war." (Job 39:25). That's a horse with a pretty sharp nose, I think, friends. Afar is a long way off.

The answer is that Job has nothing to do with it. The LORD asks, "Does the hawk take flight by your understanding…" and "Does the eagle soar at your command…" (Job 39:26-27). Each question points to the same answer: Job isn't the one behind it. The hawk's flight and the eagle's soaring don't come from his understanding or his command.

The answer is to give an answer. The LORD says, "Let him who argues with God give an answer." (Job 40:2). He's just asked, "Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty?" Now the floor is open for an answer, friends.

The answer is insignificant. Job says, "Behold, I am insignificant. How can I reply to You?" (Job 40:4). It comes after all those questions about lions, ravens and horses, friends. Then he says he places his hand over his mouth.
The answer is hand. Job says, "I place my hand over my mouth." (Job 40:4). It's a quiet picture, friends, a man who has no reply. I think I'd do the same with my mustache.

The answer is False. Job tells the LORD he has spoken once but has no answer, and twice but has "…nothing to add." (Job 40:5). After the LORD's questions about the animals, friends, Job has no answer and nothing to add.
